scale_001:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare a draft performance review competency framework for our upcoming quarterly review cycle. This is a preparatory drafting task only — leadership must review and approve the final criteria before anything is used.

First, ask me for any of the following if not already known: our company name, industry/business model, current role structure or job levels (e.g., IC1-IC5, Manager, Director), our stated company values or mission (if documented anywhere, e.g., a website or handbook), and whether we want separate competency sets per department (engineering, sales, ops, etc.) or one universal framework with role-specific additions.

Using that input, draft a structured competency framework document containing:
1. 4-7 core competencies that apply company-wide (e.g., communication, ownership, collaboration, execution) with a 1-2 sentence definition for each.
2. Role-specific or level-specific competencies (e.g., technical depth for engineers, pipeline management for sales) if applicable.
3. A simple rating scale (e.g., 1-5 or below/meets/exceeds expectations) with a short behavioral description for each rating level per competency.
4. A short rationale note explaining how each competency ties to our stated values or business priorities, so leadership can evaluate fit.

Present this as a clean, organized draft document (headings, bullet points) I can review and edit directly. Do not publish, distribute, load into any HR system, or notify anyone about this draft — it is for internal leadership review only.

When finished, summarize what you drafted, note any assumptions you made due to missing information, and clearly state that this must go through leadership review and approval, and then stop for human sign-off.

scale_001:n2.prompt:
You are helping me configure quarterly performance review templates in BambooHR ahead of our review cycle launch. Please do the following:

1. If you don't already have them, ask me for: our BambooHR domain/subdomain, confirmation you can use my configured credentials to access the BambooHR Performance module, and any existing review template names or structure I want reused or replaced.
2. Using the BambooHR Performance settings, review the current review template configuration and identify what exists today (e.g., prior quarterly templates, question sets, rating scales).
3. Draft three review template components for the new quarterly cycle: (a) a self-assessment template, (b) a manager review template, and (c) a calibration/summary template if BambooHR supports one. For each, prepare the section headings, sample questions, and rating scale you'd propose, keeping them consistent with standard quarterly performance review practice (goal review, competencies, growth areas, overall rating).
4. Prepare these as a clear draft document or checklist showing exactly what will be created or changed in BambooHR — do not create or save the templates in BambooHR yet.
5. Note any settings decisions that need my input (e.g., whether self-assessment is required before manager review starts, whether ratings are numeric or descriptive, visibility settings).

Done looks like: a complete, ready-to-apply draft of all three template types with sections, questions, and rating scales, plus a short list of open decisions for me to confirm.

Since this step requires a human to explicitly approve changes before they are applied, do not create, save, publish, or activate anything in BambooHR. Present the drafts and checklist, then stop for human sign-off, awaiting my explicit approval before you configure anything live in the system.

scale_001:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the self-assessment form distribution for our quarterly performance review cycle in BambooHR. Use my configured BambooHR credentials to access the account. If you don't already have them, ask me for: (1) our BambooHR company domain/subdomain, (2) the name of the performance review cycle already set up (or the cycle ID) that these self-assessments belong to, (3) the list of employees or the employee group/department that should receive the self-assessment form, (4) the due date for submissions, and (5) the specific self-assessment template to use if there is more than one.

Once you have this information, do the following: locate the review cycle in BambooHR's Performance module, confirm the self-assessment template and due date are correctly configured, and prepare the list of recipients by cross-checking it against the employee directory to catch any missing or inactive employees. Draft the notification/reminder message text that will accompany the self-assessment request, and compile a summary showing: cycle name, due date, template used, and the full recipient list with any discrepancies flagged.

Do not send the self-assessment forms or trigger any notifications yet. Because this step requires a human to explicitly approve before changes are applied, present the completed recipient list, template confirmation, and draft message to me for review and then stop for human sign-off. Report back with the summary, any flagged issues (e.g., employees missing from the cycle, duplicate entries, or an inactive template), and wait for my explicit approval before taking any further action in BambooHR.

scale_001:n4.prompt:
You are helping me track completion of the 'employees complete self-assessments' step in our quarterly performance review cycle. The actual writing of each self-assessment remains a human step — only each employee can produce their own honest reflection, and you cannot do this on their behalf. Your job is to prepare and monitor, not to write or submit assessments for anyone.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already provided: (1) the full list of employees expected to complete a self-assessment this cycle, (2) the deadline date, (3) the tool or system where self-assessments are collected (e.g., a shared document, spreadsheet, Google Form, or HR platform like BambooHR or Lattice), and (4) how I'd like reminders delivered (email, Slack, etc.).

Using your configured credentials, check the collection tool/system to determine which employees have submitted their self-assessment and which have not. Build a simple status tracker (a table listing employee name, submitted yes/no, and submission date if available). For anyone missing as the deadline approaches, draft a polite reminder message referencing the deadline and instructions for submitting.

Do not send reminders, mark anyone as complete, or take any action that finalizes or approves the review cycle on my behalf — prepare the drafts and status tracker, then stop for human sign-off so I can review and personally send reminders or make exceptions.

Report back with: the current completion tracker (submitted/not submitted per employee), the drafted reminder text, and a note confirming that final reminder sending and any escalation decisions remain mine to execute, since this step remains a human step until each employee completes their own assessment.

scale_001:n5.prompt:
You are helping me prepare for the 'Managers write reviews' step of our quarterly performance review cycle. This step requires each manager's firsthand judgment, so you cannot write or finalize the reviews yourself — your job is to prepare drafts and materials, then stop for human sign-off.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: the list of managers and their direct reports, the review template/questions we're using, the deadline for review submission, and where source material lives (e.g., our HRIS system, a shared drive, self-assessment docs, prior review notes, or performance data exports). Use my configured credentials to pull this information if it's accessible via an already-connected tool.

Then, for each manager/employee pair:
1. Gather any available inputs — self-assessments, prior quarter's review, goals/OKRs, relevant notes or feedback — and compile them into a single reference packet per employee.
2. Draft a skeleton review narrative using the review template, populating factual/observational sections (goals met, projects completed, feedback received) but explicitly leaving ratings and evaluative judgments blank or marked "[MANAGER TO COMPLETE]".
3. Create a checklist per manager listing which employee reviews are drafted, which inputs are missing, and the submission deadline.

Since this is an async, person-driven step, note that the actual writing and rating happens outside your control — track status by periodically checking (polling) the system where completed reviews are submitted or stored, and flag which reviews are still outstanding as the deadline approaches.

When done, report back: (1) the list of draft packets created per manager/employee, (2) any missing inputs you flagged, (3) the current submission status per manager, and confirm that no ratings or evaluative content were filled in by you — that remains a human step, and you are stopping here for human sign-off before any review is finalized or sent.

scale_001:n6.prompt:
You are helping me prepare for the calibration meeting step of our quarterly performance review cycle. The actual live discussion where managers negotiate and reconcile differing ratings across teams remains a human step — you cannot attend or facilitate it. Your job is to prepare all supporting materials so the meeting runs smoothly.

Please ask me for anything missing: (1) location of completed self-assessments and manager reviews (e.g., a shared drive, spreadsheet, or HR system export), (2) the rating scale we use, (3) list of managers/teams participating, (4) any target distribution guidelines (e.g., forced ranking or bell curve expectations), and (5) date/time of the meeting.

Once you have this, produce:
1. A consolidated calibration spreadsheet or document listing each employee, their self-assessment rating, manager's proposed rating, team, and manager name — organized for easy cross-team comparison.
2. A flagged list of outliers: employees whose ratings diverge significantly from peers in similar roles/levels, or where self-assessment and manager rating differ sharply.
3. A one-page agenda for the meeting: order of teams/employees to discuss, time allocations, and discussion prompts for contested ratings.
4. A summary of distribution stats (counts per rating tier per team) to help managers see imbalances at a glance.
5. A blank notes template for capturing final agreed ratings and rationale during the meeting.

Do not draft or send any final rating decisions, and do not modify any employee's official rating record — those changes must wait until after the live meeting concludes and a human explicitly approves the outcomes. Compile the materials, save them in a clearly labeled folder or document, and then stop for human sign-off. Report back with a summary of what you prepared, where it's stored, and the list of flagged outliers needing discussion.

scale_001:n7.prompt:
You are helping me deliver this quarter's performance reviews and schedule the follow-up 1:1s, using {{vendor}} as our team chat. The self-assessments, manager reviews, and calibration are already finished. This step covers only delivering the final reviews and booking the conversations.

Ask me for anything below that is missing:
- The list of employees, their managers, and where each finalized review document is stored.
- Whether reviews should go by direct message or in a private channel per employee.
- The 1:1 window (date range and meeting length) and whether meetings should be audio or video calls in {{vendor}}.
- Any wording or tone guidance for the delivery message.

Actions:
1. Connect to {{vendor}} through its official API and use your configured credentials. Confirm the scopes allow reading and posting messages, then tell me if any are missing.
2. For each employee, draft a short, private delivery message. It should link to their review and invite them to a 1:1 with their manager. If I chose private channels, plan the channel name and its members (employee plus manager only).
3. Propose a 1:1 slot for each employee within my window. Note how the call will be started directly from the DM or channel in {{vendor}}.
4. Optionally, draft a recurring reminder workflow in {{vendor}} that nudges managers before each 1:1. Draft it only; do not activate it.
5. Put everything into one review table with these columns: employee, manager, destination (DM or channel), message text, proposed 1:1 time, and reminder setup.

Then stop for human sign-off. Do not post messages, create channels, or activate workflows until I explicitly approve the table. After I approve, post only the approved items and confirm that each one succeeded.

Done looks like this: every employee has a delivered review message and a scheduled 1:1, with nothing posted to the wrong person. Report back with the final table, marking each row delivered, failed (with the error), or pending, plus any follow-ups I need to handle.
